pose: A highly detailed, macro shot of a paleontological preparation laboratory table, showcasing a single, continuous fossilized dinosaur bone intersecting a block made entirely of sandstone, masterfully displaying how different geological formations color this specific rock matrix. The sandstone matrix is divided into distinct, vibrant bands based on regional mineral chemistry: on the far left, the pale, greenish-tan sandstone of the Cloverly Formation shifts into the bright, cream-white quartz sandstone of the Navajo Sandstone. The center reveals the iconic, deep iron-oxidized terracotta red and rust-orange sandstone of the Morrison Formation. The right side transitions into the dark, chocolate-brown iron-carbonate-stained sandstone of the Hell Creek Formation, ending with a distinctive, deep lavender-purple silt-stained sandstone variant. A preparator's hand is visible using a fine air-scribe tool, carving away contrasting particles of colored sand to expose the dark, gleaming petrified bone texture. The scene is lit by crisp, clinical white task lights that make the rich spectrum of sandstone colors pop vividly for clear gameplay matching.
